# The result envelope and the change stream

Everything agentfs emits to a program. A one-shot command emits one envelope; `agentfs watch` emits a stream of records, one per line. This page is rendered from the member tables the encoders are held against and from the Go types the payloads are marshalled from, so a member described here and a member agentfs writes are the same member.

Both contracts are published as JSON Schema 2020-12 documents, generated from the same tables: `schema/report.v1.json` under `https://stxkxs.github.io/agentfs/schema/report.v1.json` and `schema/stream.v1.json` under `https://stxkxs.github.io/agentfs/schema/stream.v1.json`. The release workflow serves each from the path its own `$id` names.

Both admit members they do not declare. A build that adds a member must not make its output fail validation against the schema an earlier build published under the same version, so a consumer ignores what it does not recognize rather than refusing the document.

## The one-shot envelope

Every command run with `--format json` writes one object followed by a newline. The object is built in memory before any byte reaches the output, so a payload that cannot be marshalled fails without leaving a truncated object for a consumer to choke on.

| Member | Type | Always present | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | `string` | yes | The result format the document declares. Always `agentfs/report/v1`. |
| `kind` | `string` | yes | The command whose result this is, which selects the shape of data. One of `scan`, `validate`, `doctor`, `version`, `error`. |
| `version` | `string` | yes | The agentfs build that produced the result. |
| `root` | `string` | no | The workspace the result describes, absent when the result describes no workspace. |
| `exit` | `integer` | yes | The code the process terminates with, carried in the result so a reader of a captured file reaches the verdict the process reached. One of `0`, `1`, `2`, `3`, `70`, `130`. |
| `data` | `object` | no | The payload kind selects, absent for a result that carries none. |
| `diagnostics` | `array` of `diagnostic` | yes | Every finding the command accumulated, an empty array for a run that raised none. |

`schema`, `kind`, `version` and `exit` are the stable frame: they carry the same meaning in every version of this format. A consumer that meets a `schema` it does not implement can still report the `kind` and the `exit` it found, rather than failing somewhere inside a payload it half-recognized.

`diagnostics` is always present, an empty array included, so a consumer iterates it without first testing whether the key is there. `root` and `data` are absent rather than null when the result has nothing to put in them. `exit` is the status the process terminates with; [exit-codes.md](exit-codes.md) says what each one means.

One result, indented for reading — the encoder writes it as a single line:

```json
{
  "schema": "agentfs/report/v1",
  "kind": "validate",
  "version": "1.4.0",
  "root": "/srv/agents",
  "exit": 1,
  "data": {
    "schema": "agentfs/v1",
    "documents": 4,
    "errors": 1,
    "warnings": 2
  },
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "code": "AFS3002",
      "severity": "error",
      "path": "indexer/state.json",
      "pointer": "/status",
      "line": 1,
      "column": 36,
      "message": "The status \"not running\" is not in the contract vocabulary.",
      "hint": "Use one of: running, idle, blocked, error, done. Matching is exact, not by substring.",
      "value": "not running"
    }
  ]
}
```

## A diagnostic

Every finding agentfs reports has this shape, in the envelope's `diagnostics` member and under each agent of a scan result. Branch on `code` and `pointer`. [diagnostics.md](diagnostics.md) is the registry: what each code means, the severity it is raised at, and which codes no JSON Schema validator can produce.

| Member | Type | Always present | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `string` | yes | The finding's permanent identifier, which is what a consumer branches on. A code is retired rather than reused. One of the codes in [diagnostics.md](diagnostics.md). |
| `severity` | `string` | yes | How serious the finding is. A document carrying an error is not usable as state. One of `info`, `warning`, `error`. |
| `path` | `string` | no | The workspace-relative path of the document the finding is about, absent for a finding about the workspace itself. |
| `pointer` | `string` | no | An RFC 6901 pointer to the member the finding is about, absent when the finding is about the document as a whole. Abbreviated to 200 runes. |
| `line` | `integer` | no | The 1-based line of pointer within the document, absent when the position does not resolve. |
| `column` | `integer` | no | The 1-based column of pointer within the document, absent when the position does not resolve. |
| `message` | `string` | yes | Prose naming the condition, for a person to read. It carries no contract and is reworded without a schema version. |
| `hint` | `string` | no | Prose naming the edit that resolves the finding. Applying it to the document makes the finding go away. |
| `value` | `string` | no | The offending value prepared for display: a terminal control sequence is replaced by a visible marker, a rune that reorders or hides the text around it is replaced by a visible stand-in, and the text is abbreviated to the ceiling. It does not reproduce the document's bytes. Abbreviated to 120 runes. |

`value` is prepared for display rather than reproduced: a terminal control sequence is replaced by a visible marker, a rune that reorders or hides the text around it is replaced by a visible stand-in, and a value past the ceiling is abbreviated with a trailing ellipsis. A value its message also quotes carries any quotation mark of its own as an apostrophe, so the quoted run and the value read the same. A consumer that needs the offending bytes reads them from the document at `path`, `line` and `column`.

`message` and `hint` are prose for a person. They are reworded without a schema version, so a consumer that matches on their text breaks on a release that carries no contract change.

## What `data` holds, by kind

One section per value of `kind`. A consumer selects the shape from the kind rather than by probing the payload.

### The `scan` result

One reading of the workspace: what each agent declares, and the findings about the workspace itself.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agents` | `array` | One object per detected agent workspace, ordered by name. See the agent table below. |
| `diagnostics` | `array` | Findings about the workspace itself rather than about one document, absent when there are none. A scan repeats exactly these in the envelope's own diagnostics member; a finding about one document is reached through that agent's entry instead. |
| `observed_at` | `string` | When the scan read the workspace, RFC 3339 with its offset. It is the observer's clock, not the agent's, and it is what every age in the result is measured against. |

### An agent in a `scan` result

One detected agent workspace. Read `presence` before anything else: it says how the declaration below it is known, and only `declared` carries a reading to act on.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | The agent's name: the `agent` member of its state document, or the workspace directory name when the document declares none. |
| `dir` | `string` | The workspace-relative directory the agent occupies. |
| `presence` | `string` | How the state below is known. |
| `state` | `object` | The decoded declaration. Under a presence of `settling` it is the last reading that decoded, not the reading being observed. |
| `diagnostics` | `array` | Findings this agent's document raised, absent when it raised none. A scan leaves them here rather than in the envelope's diagnostics member. |
| `document` | `string` | The workspace-relative path of the state document, absent when the directory declares none. |
| `age` | `integer` | How long since the agent declared it wrote the document, as a count of nanoseconds. It is measured from `updated_at`, falling back to `started_at`, against `observed_at`. Zero when the document declares neither timestamp, and negative when a document is stamped further ahead of the observer's clock than the skew tolerance absorbs. |
| `roles` | `array` | The conventional subdirectories the workspace carries, absent when it carries none. |

`presence` is one of `absent`, `declared`, `stale`, `settling`, `invalid`, `unreadable`. Only `declared` is a reading to act on: a `status` of `unknown` under a presence of `invalid` means the document did not decode, which is a different fact from an agent that declared itself idle.

`state` is the document the agent wrote, decoded. Its members are the state contract, which [state-schema.md](state-schema.md) describes and `schema/agent-state.v1.json` publishes.

### The `validate` result

The tally of a conformance run. Every finding it counts is in the envelope's diagnostics member, including the findings about individual documents that a scan leaves under each agent.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | `string` | The contract version the documents were read against. |
| `documents` | `integer` | The number of agent workspaces examined. |
| `errors` | `integer` | How many diagnostics are at error severity. A non-zero count is what makes the command exit 1. |
| `warnings` | `integer` | How many diagnostics are at warning severity. Under `--strict` a warning is counted as an error instead. |

### The `doctor` result

How this workspace is observed and what observing it costs. The numbers are what agentfs measured on this root, not defaults.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `root` | `string` | The workspace the check ran against. |
| `filesystem` | `string` | What the root was probed as, in the name the platform reports. |
| `filesystem_kind` | `string` | The class the probed type falls into, which is what selects a detection mechanism. |
| `events_complete` | `boolean` | Whether kernel notification observes a write made by another client of this filesystem. False means a sweep is required to see one. |
| `mode` | `string` | The resolved detection mechanism. |
| `agents` | `integer` | How many agent workspaces the root holds. |
| `nodes` | `integer` | How many filesystem nodes the bounded survey retained. |
| `directories_read` | `integer` | How many directory reads the survey spent. |
| `tracked_dirs` | `integer` | How many directories a sweep covers. |
| `sweep_budget` | `integer` | How many of the tracked directories one sweep cycle reads. A set larger than the budget is covered across successive cycles. |
| `sweep_interval` | `string` | How long one sweep cycle waits, as a Go duration string such as `2s`. |
| `watch_budget` | `integer` | The ceiling on kernel watches this process holds. |
| `confinement` | `string` | The sandbox the process runs under, as far as it can determine. |
| `schema_version` | `string` | The state contract this build enforces. |
| `operations_per_hour` | `integer` | The ceiling on filesystem operations this process spends sweeping, per hour. Zero under a mode that does not sweep. Multiply by the number of instances pointed at one shared export. |

### The `version` result

The identity of the binary that produced the result. The envelope's own version member repeats the version from here.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `string` | The released version without its leading `v`, or `dev` for a build made outside a release. |
| `commit` | `string` | The revision the build was made from, or `unknown`. A build from a tree carrying uncommitted changes is suffixed `-dirty`. |
| `build_date` | `string` | When the binary was built, RFC 3339 in UTC, or `unknown`. |
| `go_version` | `string` | The toolchain that compiled the binary. |
| `schema` | `string` | The state contract this build implements, read from the contract itself. |

### The `error` result

A command that could not produce a result carries no payload. The exit member names the reason and the diagnostics describe it: a root that could not be read arrives as `AFS5010` with the path in its value. Reading this kind the same way as any other is what keeps a consumer from needing a second parser for the one path where the command failed.

## The change-stream record

`agentfs watch --format ndjson` writes one record per line and keeps writing until it is interrupted or a write fails. Each line is a complete JSON object; the stream as a whole is not one, so a validator is pointed at a line.

| Member | Type | Always present | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | `string` | yes | The record format the line declares. Always `agentfs/stream/v1`. |
| `kind` | `string` | yes | What the record reports, which selects the shape of data. One of `change`, `status`, `error`. |
| `seq` | `integer` | yes | The producer's record ordinal, counting from 1, so a gap names a record the consumer did not receive. |
| `time` | `string` | yes | The instant the record reports, RFC 3339 with its offset. |
| `dedup_key` | `string` | no | The identity of the event the record reports, absent for a record that reports no repeatable event. |
| `data` | `object` | no | The payload kind selects, absent for a record that carries none. |

The stream is at-least-once. The two identifiers answer different questions: `seq` orders the records one producer emitted and exposes a loss as a gap, and `dedup_key` names the underlying event, so a consumer discards a repeat by key. A producer that restarts begins its sequence again at 1 and emits the same keys, which is why a consumer that treats `seq` as an identity double-counts across a restart.

`dedup_key` is built from what the record reports, with a NUL between the parts. For a change it is the workspace-relative path and the operation. For a status record it is the record's instant in RFC 3339 and the event name; for an error record, the instant and the message. The NUL arrives as `\u0000` because the JSON encoder escapes it — a consumer compares the decoded string and never has to parse it.

One record, indented for reading — the encoder writes it as a single line:

```json
{
  "schema": "agentfs/stream/v1",
  "kind": "change",
  "seq": 1,
  "time": "2026-04-08T13:00:00Z",
  "dedup_key": "indexer/state.json\u0000modify",
  "data": {
    "path": "indexer/state.json",
    "op": "modify",
    "is_dir": false
  }
}
```

## What a record's `data` holds, by kind

### The `change` record

One path changed. The record says that it changed, not what it now holds: the consumer re-reads the paths it cares about, which is what keeps the producer's cost independent of what the workspace writes.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | The path that changed, workspace-relative and slash-separated. A change whose path escapes the root is dropped at the source rather than delivered. |
| `op` | `string` | What happened to it. |
| `is_dir` | `boolean` | Whether the path is a directory, as far as the source could tell. A removal cannot state it, so a removal reports false. |

`op` is one of `create`, `modify`, `remove`, `rename`. Only kernel notification reports `rename`, at the path renamed away from; a sweep reports the same rename as a removal at the old path and a creation at the new one. A consumer that re-reads the paths a record names handles both without telling them apart.

### The `status` record

The stream's own condition: what it is watching, and every way it can be falling behind. The counters are cumulative for the producer's lifetime, so a consumer reads them to size a loss rather than to detect one — a loss is announced by an event.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event` | `string` | The condition this record reports. |
| `watching` | `string` | The workspace root. |
| `mode` | `string` | The resolved detection mechanism. |
| `filesystem` | `string` | What the root was probed as. |
| `tracked` | `integer` | How many directories the sweep covers, zero under a mode that does not sweep. |
| `watches` | `integer` | How many kernel watches the producer holds. |
| `watches_refused` | `integer` | How many directories the budget or the kernel refused a watch for. Changes below them are seen by sweep or not at all. |
| `coalesced` | `integer` | How many changes were folded into another change on the same path. |
| `deduplicated` | `integer` | How many changes were discarded because another source had already reported them. |
| `dropped` | `integer` | How many changes were lost to a batch ceiling. Every drop is accompanied by a `resync` event. |
| `errors` | `integer` | How many source faults the producer has observed. A rise in it writes one error record carrying the new total, so a single record can account for several faults. |

`event` is one of `opened`, `resync`, `root_lost` or `root_recovered`. Each record names one condition, so a batch that both recovers a root and demands a resync writes one record for each. A `resync` means the changes delivered before it are not a complete account: rebuild from the filesystem rather than applying what came before.

### The `error` record

A fault the producer met and could not resolve, such as a tracked directory it cannot read. The stream continues: a fault is reported once, when the count rises past what has been reported.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | What the source reported. |
| `count` | `integer` | How many faults this producer has observed, the reported one included. |
